B. Is this measure already running in North Savo wellbeing services county (or in the KYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: In a Dutch national registry study of elderly stage I patients, the share left untreated fell by 7 percentage points once stereotactic radiotherapy was fully available, but the study does not report the change as a share of all lung cancer patients.
supported_en: Haasbeek et al. (Annals of Oncology, 2012): 7% fewer elderly stage I patients in the Netherlands went untreated after stereotactic radiotherapy became available.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show the 0.8-point gain in the share of all patients treated with curative intent, or any Finnish or KYS baseline for it.
in_use_quote: Jos kyseessä on pieni keuhkotuumori eikä kasvain ole paikallisesti edennyt, voidaan antaa täsmäsädehoitoa mikäli potilaan yleistila tai muut sairaudet eivät salli operatiivista hoitoa.
missing_en: No page we read sets a rule that every stage I patient too frail for surgery must be referred for stereotactic radiotherapy, or measures whether this happens.
summary_en: The KYS lung cancer care chain, published by KYS Cancer Centre (PDF version 1.2, dated 2021), says that a small lung tumour that has not spread locally can be treated with precision radiotherapy if the patient's health does not allow surgery. The Suomi.fi service page of the North Savo wellbeing services county (updated 9.10.2026) says KYS gives radiotherapy at its radiotherapy hospital in Kuopio. For the effect, a Dutch national registry study found 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated after stereotactic radiotherapy became available; this backs the direction of the effect, but the 0.8-point gain across all patients remains our own assumption.
unanswered_en: We found no published referral rule or audit showing how many frail stage I patients at KYS get stereotactic radiotherapy and how many go untreated.
